title: Usage record
description: Token counts for one provider call. A field the provider does not report is null, never 0 (R4): a missing count and a measured zero are different facts, and collapsing them is how a structurally-zero column gets published as a measurement. The names here are the transport's own; the provider-specific names they map onto were frozen by U1's live capture rather than assumed, and the mapping is not what the provider's own nesting suggests -- see the per-field notes.

prompt_tokens.description: Input tokens, from the provider's `prompt_tokens`. null when the provider does not report it.

completion_tokens.description: Output tokens, from the provider's `completion_tokens`. null when the provider does not report it.

reasoning_tokens.description: Reasoning tokens, from the provider's `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. Measured, not assumed: this is a SUBSET of completion_tokens. A captured completion reporting completion_tokens=18 with reasoning_tokens=15 contained three tokens of content, so adding the two double-counts and omitting it under-reports. It also sits one level deeper than the other fields, which is exactly why a hand-written mapping would have got it wrong.

cached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache, from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. Priced differently from uncached input, so a row that conflates them mis-prices the call. The provider also reports `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` and `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`, which carry the same information; they are deliberately not normalized into a second and third field here, because two more homes for one fact is how one of them drifts.

total_tokens.description: The provider's own total, retained as an external check on the arithmetic. The aggregate sums the fields above, and comparing that sum to a number the provider computed is the only place token accounting can be validated against something other than itself. KTD7 wanted exactly that for cost and could not have it -- the provider reports no cost field -- which makes this the one such check available, and discarding it would leave the accounting certifying itself.
